title: SliceBench: kernel sensitivity sweep for quant profiles (throughput vs fidelity)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build and run a new benchmarking harness (SliceBench) that measures how kernel selection and quantization profiles (FP16 / INT8 / INT4) affect tokens/sec and p95 latency while tracking quality regressions on realistic workloads. This ticket covers design, infra, experiments, and automated regression detection.

Scope:
- Implement a workload slicing mechanism that runs representative buckets (short chat prompts, long-context completions, high-entropy code-generation) to surface long-tail perf/quality trade-offs.
- Sweep kernel choices (e.g., fused attention vs tiled matmul, int4-friendly kernels) across quant profiles and batching configurations.
- Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and KV-cache hit effects.
- Evaluate quality using a compact eval set (ROUGE/EM-style tasks, embedding cosine similarity, and a prompt-level fidelity score derived from token-level KL/fluency heuristics).
- Integrate with the regression detector: automatic alerting when throughput drops >10% or fidelity metric decreases beyond per-profile thresholds.
- Produce a dashboard with heatmaps and scatter plots to guide model/kernel recommendations and autotuning knobs.

Acceptance criteria:
- SliceBench can run end-to-end on dedicated test pool and produce reproducible CSV outputs for each slice.
- Regression detector flags regressions per-profile and posts a summary artifact to the runtime-telemetry S3 path.
- A first sweep (FP16/INT8/INT4) has been executed and results summarized in a design doc with recommended default kernel/profile pairings and suggested guardrails for Canary rollouts.
tasks: Design slice taxonomy and choose 6 representative prompt buckets (chat-short, chat-long, code, instruction, summarization, retrieval-augmented)
Implement slice runner that locks sequence length distribution and seed for deterministic sampling

Instrument metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU occupancy, memory footprint, KV-cache hit rate
Create compact quality eval and scoring script (embedding-similarity + token-level KL)
Wire regression detector with threshold config and Slack/webhook alerting
Publish dashboard: heatmap of throughput vs fidelity for each quant/kernel combination
Run baseline sweep and capture artifacts, then write PRD summary and next steps
